data.narrative:
DefSecIntel is a Series A-stage defense and security technology company. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of three same-sector, same-stage private companies (Stark Defence, Singularity, and NODA AI) alongside a broader comp set of ten private firms and two public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS).

The peer-median method, the primary applicable triangulation approach given available data, yields a $400M implied valuation. This reflects the median across the three direct comparables, which range from $125M (NODA AI) to $4.0B (Stark Defence). The wide dispersion—a 32x spread between floor and ceiling—reflects material heterogeneity within Series A defense tech, likely driven by differences in technical maturity, customer traction, and IP positioning. The broader comp set includes later-stage peers (Anduril Industries, Helsing) and public-market data points, which contextualize but do not directly anchor this estimate given stage mismatch.

The triangulated valuation range is $340M to $460M, centered on the $400M median. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method across a limited peer sample. Key uncertainties include DefSecIntel's revenue run-rate and customer concentration relative to comparables, capital efficiency relative to defense-sector norms, and defensibility of core IP. Validation of this range would require detailed benchmarking against peer unit economics and customer acquisition costs.
